Reporting Landscape
How We Report and Create Value
1GRI 2-3
Coromandel International Limited (hereinafter referred 
to as “the Company”, “CIL”, or “Coromandel”) presents 
its Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26. The 
Report covers the Company’s financial, operational 
and environmental, social and governance (ESG) 
performance.
The objective of this Report is to provide a concise 
and integrated overview of Coromandel’s strategy, 
governance, performance and value creation process 
across financial and non financial capitals, enabling 
stakeholders to understand how the Company creates 
sustainable long term value.
Our Approach to Integrated Reporting
Coromandel International Limited (CIL) is one of India’s 
leading agri solutions providers, operating across the 
agricultural value chain with a focus on innovation, 
operational excellence and responsible practices.
This Integrated Report presents the Company’s 
financial and non financial performance for the year 
ended March 31, 2026, and articulates how Coromandel 
creates sustainable value for its stakeholders in 
alignment with its Vision, Mission and Values.
Coromandel’s integrated reporting approach brings 
together financial disclosures with environmental, 
social and governance (ESG) performance, enhancing 
transparency, 
comparability 
and 
decision 
useful 
insights for stakeholders, in line with leading global 
reporting practices.
Reporting Principles
This 
Integrated 
Report 
has 
been 
prepared 
in 
accordance with the principles of the International 
Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC). The disclosures are 
also aligned with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) 
Standards and comply with the requirements of India’s 
Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting 
(BRSR) framework.
Through this approach, the Report supports alignment 
with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
(UN SDGs) and reflects Coromandel’s commitment 
to transparent, relevant and globally comparable 
reporting.
Materiality
Coromandel identifies its material topics through a 
structured assessment process involving stakeholder 
engagement and internal evaluations. These topics are 
prioritised based on their relevance to the Company’s 
business strategy, long term value creation and 
stakeholder interests.
The identified material matters are evaluated with 
reference to globally recognised frameworks such as 
the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), 
Dow Jones Sustainability Index (DJSI) and MSCI, 
ensuring comprehensive coverage of both financial and 
non financial impacts.
During 
FY 2025–26, 
Coromandel 
conducted 
a 
comprehensive materiality assessment exercise, the 
details and outcomes of which are presented in the 
section below.
Inclusivity
Coromandel emphasises accountability towards all 
stakeholders impacted directly or indirectly by its 
operations. Through structured stakeholder mapping, 
engagement and feedback mechanisms, the Company 
integrates stakeholder expectations into its strategy, 
decision making and operations.
CIL continues to strengthen engagement across 
corporate, manufacturing, supply chain and marketing 
functions to foster collaboration and drive continuous 
improvement.
Scope and Reporting Boundary
This Integrated Report presents information for 
Coromandel International Limited on a standalone 
basis and covers all facilities operated by the Company 
across its businesses, including Fertilisers, Specialty 
Nutrients, Crop Protection, Retail and Specialty 
Chemicals.
Unless otherwise specified, the disclosures relate to 
Coromandel’s operations within India and encompass its 
economic, social and environmental performance. The 
reporting boundary extends to factors that materially 
influence the Company’s ability to create sustainable 
value over the short, medium and long term.
Reporting Period
This 
Integrated 
Report 
covers 
the 
period 
from 
April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. The Report is published 
on an annual basis.
Reliability of Data
Coromandel follows a robust verification framework 
to ensure the accuracy, completeness and reliability of 
information disclosed in this Report. The disclosures 
are supported by internal controls, periodic reviews and 
defined audit trails.
ESG data has been subjected to external assurance 
in accordance with the GRI Guidelines and ISAE 3000 
(revised), while BRSR Core disclosures have been 
assured in line with BRSR Assurance requirements and 
ISAE 3000 (revised), enhancing the credibility of the 
reported information.
Responsibility and Feedback Statement
The Report has been developed under the guidance and 
oversight of Coromandel’s Board of Directors in adherence 
to 
applicable 
regulatory 
frameworks. 
Stakeholder 
feedback is valued and welcomed to strengthen future 
disclosures.

Reflections from 
the Leadership
For more than six decades, Coromandel has been built 
on a simple conviction shared with the wider Murugappa 
Group: enduring growth comes from strong foundations, 
disciplined execution and the willingness to invest 
ahead of the curve. FY2025-26 reflected all three. In 
a year marked by external volatility, we continued to 
strengthen our core businesses, deliver on important 
strategic investments and build the capabilities required 
for the future. As several of these investments now move 
from execution to commissioning and operationalisation, 
our priorities are sharply defined: to translate them into 
value, stronger returns and sustainable cash flows, 
while continuing to scale the businesses that will shape 
Coromandel’s next phase of growth.
Operating Context: Opportunity Amid Volatility
The year combined opportunity with uncertainty. 
India remained the fastest-growing large economy, 
agriculture benefited from record sowing and record 
foodgrain production, and policy continuity continued to 
support the farm sector. At the same time, the operating 
environment was far from benign. Rupee depreciation, 
raw material inflation, subsidy mismatches and, toward 
the close of the year, the rapidly evolving Middle East 
crisis created significant pressure across fertiliser and 
crop protection value chains. We also continue to engage 
constructively with the Government on the need for a 
more responsive Nutrient Based Subsidy framework 
that keeps pace with input cost realities and supports 
the long-term sustainability of the phosphatic industry.
In such an environment, disciplined execution, supply 
assurance and operating resilience assumed even 
greater importance. It is in periods such as these that the 
strength of an integrated business model, the quality 
of manufacturing assets and the depth of management 
capability are truly tested. 
Dear Shareholders
Performance with Resilience
Against this backdrop, Coromandel delivered another 
year of strong performance. On a standalone basis, 
FY26 revenue stood at about Rs. 30,531 crore and PAT 
at about Rs. 2,009 crore, with consolidated performance 
reflecting the contribution of our retail, Nano, Bio and 
the recently acquired NACL businesses. We recorded 
complex fertiliser sales of 42.8 lakh metric tonnes and 
SSP sales of 8.4 lakh metric tonnes during the year.
A defining milestone was Coromandel’s emergence as 
India’s largest phosphatic fertiliser company by PoS sales 
volume for the second consecutive year in FY26. This 
achievement is a significant validation of the Company’s 
long-standing investments in its phosphatic platform, 
manufacturing capabilities, market presence and deep 
farmer connect.
These outcomes represent more than a good set of 
annual numbers. They reflect the resilience of our 
business model, the strength of our market position 
and our ability to perform with consistency through a 
demanding external environment. They also reinforce 
our conviction that Coromandel’s long-term strategy 
remains firmly on track.
Delivering on our Investment Agenda
A defining priority during the year was execution. 
Over the last few years, Coromandel has committed 
substantial capital toward strengthening its core 
manufacturing and integration platform. Between FY21 
and FY26, the Company made investment commitments 
for organic and inorganic expansion of close to Rs. 7,000 
Message from 
Executive Chairman
crore, one of the most ambitious capital deployment 
cycles in Coromandel’s history. FY26 saw a number of 
these investments reach important milestones.
Our Phosphoric Acid and Sulphuric Acid plants at 
Kakinada were completed in March 2026. Our 9,000 MT 
Mancozeb project at Dahej was commissioned in January 
2026. Earlier investments have also begun to translate 
into tangible value. The sulphuric acid plant at Vizag 
commissioned in FY24 has already generated savings of 
nearly Rs. 400 crore, while the Dahej Mancozeb project 
has started yielding returns in line with the original 
investment plan.
The significance of these developments lies not merely 
in asset creation, but in what they now enable. The next 
phase for Coromandel is not about investing for the sake 
of scale. It is about ensuring that these investments 
deliver the benefits for which they were conceived: 
stronger margins, improved operating leverage, greater 
import substitution, better integration and healthier cash 
generation.
We are applying the same discipline to projects under 
execution. The H-Train at Kakinada is progressing 
in line with its Q4 FY2027 timeline. The 17,500 MT 
Mancozeb project at Sarigam is advancing as scheduled. 
The 
technical-grade 
Mono-Ammonium 
Phosphate 
(tMAP) plant at Vizag is also moving ahead as planned. 
Alongside these, we have progressed the StuccoEdge 
joint venture with for gypsum plaster, which will create 
productive value from phospho-gypsum and extend 
value extraction from our phosphatics chain.
Timely and safe execution of these investments will 
remain a top management priority. Equally important, 
we are sharply focused on realising the benefits 
envisaged from the investments already made. After a 
period of significant capital deployment, Coromandel 
is now entering a phase where value realisation, asset 
productivity and cash flow discipline assume even 
greater importance.
Taken together, these developments mark an important 
shift in our journey. After several years of building the 
core and investing in future platforms, we are now 
moving into the next phase with a clear strategic 
direction: Consolidate to Accelerate.
Managing Supply Chain Volatility and Protecting 
Input Security
Even the strongest internal momentum must reckon 
with an external environment that is rarely entirely 
cooperative. The escalation in the Middle East created 
a direct operating challenge for the agri-inputs sector. 
India remains significantly dependent on imported 
ammonia, urea, DAP and sulphur routed through the 
Strait of Hormuz, while crop protection is also exposed 
to petroleum and gas-linked raw materials. We have 
viewed this not as a reason to lose strategic momentum, 
but as an external challenge to be actively managed 
through a combination of short-term agility and long-
term structural de-risking.
Operationally, 
we 
have 
prioritised 
procurement 
optimisation, 
prudent 
shipment 
planning, 
higher 
utilisation of captive phosphoric acid and active policy 
engagement. Initiation of trial production of Kakinada 
Phosphoric Acid and Sulphuric Acid, the stabilisation 
of Senegal BMCC mining operations and our green 
ammonia arrangements are progressively reducing 
vulnerability and improving input security for the core 
fertiliser business. This combination underlines why 
backward integration, manufacturing strength and 
supply chain resilience remain central to Coromandel’s 
strategy.
Scaling the Growth Engines
As we consolidate the core, we are also accelerating the 
businesses that will drive our next phase of growth.
In crop protection, FY26 was a year of strong momentum. 
CPC EBITDA crossed Rs. 500 crore, supported by 
improved domestic B2B and export margins and aided by 
the Mancozeb platform. A significant strategic milestone 
during the year was the completion of the NACL 
acquisition. This transaction strengthens Coromandel’s 
position in the Indian agchem market and expands our 
manufacturing footprint, product portfolio and technical 
capabilities in crop protection. Since completion, our focus 
has been on disciplined integration, improving operating 
performance and strengthening NACL’s balance sheet, 
and the initial results, including a clear improvement in 
EBITDA and a stronger capital structure at NACL, are 
encouraging. We recognise that NACL’s turnaround is 
still in its early phase, and integration synergies across 
manufacturing, procurement, R&D, IT, retail and product 
movement will accrue progressively. We view NACL not 
as a standalone addition, but as a strategic platform that 
can contribute meaningfully to Coromandel’s long-term 
growth in crop protection.
Beyond crop protection, we continue to build a broader 
and more future-ready growth portfolio. Our retail 
business expanded rapidly, with a net addition of 320 
new stores during the year, taking the total store count 
to ~1200. Retail revenue grew by 31% and EBITDA by 
29%. Nano recorded 76% growth in EBITDA, while Bio 
delivered 27% EBITDA growth.
These businesses are not merely adjacent opportunities. 
They are integral to Coromandel’s evolution into a more 
diversified agri-solutions platform with deeper farmer 
engagement, a wider product portfolio and greater 
resilience across business cycles.
The Farmer at the Heart of Our Work
The numbers in this report tell one part of our story. 
The Indian farmer tells the rest. We see our work as 
a partnership in farmer prosperity, a shared value 
philosophy that sits at the centre of who we are.
Our Gromor Drive drone spray service brings this to life. 
From twenty pilots in 2022, we now operate 275 DGCA 
certified pilots, 249 drones and 158 vehicles across 95 
clusters in seven states. A single drone covers an acre 
in ten minutes with just ten litres of water, replacing 
manual spraying with a contactless, battery powered 
alternative that reduces farmer chemical exposure, 
input use and labour dependence. The same philosophy 
runs across our Nano fertilisers, Bio products, soil and

Building New Growth Avenues from our 
Phosphatic Strengths
As we look forward, a key element of our future strategy 
is to build selectively from our phosphatic chemistry 
strengths. The tMAP initiative is an important step in 
extending our phosphatic platform into differentiated 
and higher-value applications. StuccoEdge reflects our 
intent to create value from byproduct streams while 
improving circularity within the business. We are also 
evaluating further chemistry-led opportunities, including 
purified phosphoric acid and other extensions, with the 
same discipline that has guided capital allocation in the 
core business.
Our approach is straightforward. We aim to build 
adjacencies where Coromandel enjoys a natural right 
to win, drawing on process knowledge, manufacturing 
assets, integration strengths and market relevance, 
rather than diversifying opportunistically. This positions 
Coromandel not only as a scale player in phosphatic, but 
as a company capable of extracting greater value from 
its chemistry platform over time.
Investing in Digital, Analytics and Future-Ready 
Capabilities
Capability building remains another major priority. We 
continue to invest in Digital, Analytics, Instrumentation 
and AI to improve decision-making, execution quality and 
customer responsiveness. During the year, Digital Data 
Centre 2.0 went live with 621 KPIs across businesses 
and functions. Migration to SAP Rise was completed 
successfully. We also strengthened our innovation 
agenda through our partnership with IIT Madras Global 
for a Corporate Research Centre.
These investments are foundational to the next phase of 
growth. As Coromandel becomes larger, more integrated 
and more complex, institutional capability, data-led 
execution and research depth will matter as much as 
physical capacity. Our competitive edge will increasingly 
depend not only on what we manufacture, but on how 
intelligently, efficiently and responsively we operate.
Safety, Manufacturing Excellence and 
Responsible Growth
As we accelerate, safety remains paramount. We will not 
compromise on safety, process discipline or responsible 
operations in the pursuit of growth.
During the year, our Kakinada facility received the British 
Safety Council’s Sword of Honour, joining Vizag as the 
second major Coromandel plant to earn this prestigious 
recognition. Coromandel has also secured Responsible 
Care certification, placing it among a select group of 
organisations globally recognised for their commitment 
to world-class standards in safety, health, environment 
and responsible operations.
Our broader ESG and EHS priorities remain anchored in 
renewable energy, desalination, the standardisation of 
safety systems and stronger stewardship across sites. 
Manufacturing excellence and supply chain resilience 
must always rest on a foundation of safe and responsible 
operations. For Coromandel, that principle remains non-
negotiable.
Climate is among the most consequential long-term 
issues our industry will navigate. Our climate and 
sustainability agenda is being shaped around recognised 
global frameworks. We are progressively aligning our 
climate disclosures with the Task Force on Climate-
related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), advancing our 
work on nature along the principles of the Taskforce 
on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) and 
shaping our decarbonisation roadmap with reference to 
the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi). The building 
blocks are already in place, including renewable energy 
at our manufacturing sites, desalination projects that 
ease our freshwater dependence, green ammonia 
arrangements that begin to decarbonise our nitrogen 
supply and circularity initiatives such as StuccoEdge 
that draw productive value from byproduct streams. For 
us, climate action is not an initiative layered onto the 
business but integral to how we operate.
Governance, Capital Discipline and Returns to 
Shareholders
Institutional strength is built not only through projects 
and financial performance, but also through governance, 
capital discipline and the way we balance growth 
investment with returns to shareholders. Over the last 
five years, Coromandel has invested substantially in 
strengthening its business and we remain committed to 
ensuring that these investments translate into superior 
returns and sustainable value creation.
Consistent with the Company’s track record of rewarding 
shareholders, the Board has recommended a dividend of 
Rs. 11 per equity share for FY 2025-26, reflecting both 
our confidence in the business and our commitment to a 
balanced capital allocation approach, one that combines 
disciplined reinvestment in growth platforms with 
steady returns to shareholders. We will continue to be 
deliberate in scaling growth platforms, disciplined in 
capital allocation and focused on building capabilities 
that endure beyond business cycles.
Talent, Leadership and Culture
As our business evolves, our investment in leadership 
development, organisational capability and a stronger 
performance culture continues to deepen. Coromandel’s 
recognition in the Hurun India Performance Index 
and similar external benchmarks reflects the quality 
of our institutional fabric, but more importantly, the 
commitment of the teams across our plants, offices and 
field operations. These institutional strengths will be 
essential in sustaining both growth and resilience in the 
years ahead.
Looking Ahead
We remain optimistic despite near-term risks. The 
external environment may continue to be volatile, 
particularly in relation to geopolitics, raw material 
markets and subsidy dynamics. Even so, Coromandel 
enters the next phase from a position of greater strength: 
a stronger core, a deeper manufacturing base, improving 
integration, growing new businesses, stronger digital 
foundations and clearer strategic intent.
Our direction is clear. We will consolidate the core, 
accelerate the growth engines and build for the future 
with discipline, confidence and long-term purpose.

Managing Director & 
CEO’s Message
Dear Shareholders
It gives me pleasure to present to you the Annual Report 
for the financial year 2025–26. Your Company has emerged 
stronger, more resilient and better positioned to pursue 
future growth opportunities and create long-term value for 
all stakeholders.
India stood out as one of the fastest-growing major 
economies, with estimated GDP growth of 7.76%, 
supported by strong domestic drivers - particularly 
private consumption and gross fixed capital formation.
The year gone by presented its share of challenges, 
marked by trade disruptions, tariff actions and heightened 
geopolitical tensions.
The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
emerged as a defining global trend, transforming 
industries through new business models, improved 
productivity and accelerated innovation.
On the policy front, initiatives such as the overhaul of 
the Goods and Services Tax framework, implementation 
of labour codes and measures aimed at liberalising 
foreign investment, promoting exports and enhancing 
manufacturing 
competitiveness 
are 
expected 
to 
strengthen 
the 
sector’s 
global 
competitiveness. 
Government policies remained supportive of farmers 
by keeping fertilisers affordable at the farm gate and 
ensuring its timely availability throughout the year. At 
the same time, policy emphasis on balanced nutrition 
and domestic capacity expansion is strengthening long-
term soil health and supply security for the nation.
Indian agriculture received an above-normal monsoon 
boosting sowing activities and overall food grain 
production, yet a late retreat of the rains dampened 
consumption in some regions. Despite these headwinds, 
rural demand proved resilient, aided by steady 
government support through farmer income schemes, 
robust credit flow and strong procurement activities.
Towards the end of the year, the escalation of conflict 
in the Middle East emerged as a significant disruptor, 
with cascading implications for global and regional 
economies, particularly across Asia. The crisis impacted 
key trade corridors and maritime routes, leading to 
elevated freight costs, supply chain disruptions and 
delays in the movement of critical commodities including 
fertiliser intermediates and finished products, created 
periodic supply imbalances.
Coromandel: Strong performance in challenging 
times
Amidst this challenging operating environment, your 
Company delivered a robust performance, marked by 
sustained growth and stable profitability. In a year when 
the broader agricultural sector witnessed slower growth 
and pockets of subdued consumption due to climate 
variability, Coromandel’s performance underscores the 
strength of its business model, agility and disciplined 
execution.
Your company’s manufacturing operations continued 
to run safely and reliably, reaching its highest ever 
utilization levels. We reinforced our supply chain and

Strengthening backward integration in Fertilisers
During the year, Coromandel successfully commissioned a 650 TPD Phosphoric Acid plant built on advanced DA-HF 
(Dihydrate Attack-Hemihydrate Filtration) technology and supported by an automated DCS system. The Company also set 
up an 2000 TPD Sulphuric Acid plant to serve its captive needs, while utilising waste heat for power generation. As essential 
intermediates for phosphatic fertilisers such as DAP and NPKs, these investments meaningfully deepen backward integration, 
securing supply continuity and meeting a substantial share of the Kakinada plant’s acid requirements.
Creating India’s largest phosphatic fertiliser complex
The Company is on course to establish a 7.5 lakh tonne NPK granulation capacity. This will take the Kakinada site to a 
total capacity of 30 lakh tonnes, making it India’s largest phosphatic fertiliser complex. Building on earlier investments in 
phosphoric and sulphuric acid plants, the strategically located Kakinada facility will draw on its logistical advantages to 
serve markets across India efficiently, while producing high-quality, energy-efficient phosphatic fertilisers. The brownfield 
expansion is expected to be completed in FY27 and will support import substitution, particularly in the northern markets, 
thereby promoting balanced crop nutrition through NPK fertilisers.
Developing India’s first technical MAP water soluble fertiliser plant
Coromandel is advancing its innovation-led growth strategy through the development of India’s first technical MAP (Mono 
Ammonium Phosphate) water soluble fertiliser plant. This will strengthen the Company’s presence in the high-value specialty 
nutrients segment, catering to the growing demand for precision farming and fertigation solutions. With India currently 
dependent on imports for its entire MAP requirement, the project will enable import substitution, ensure reliable availability 
of high-quality MAP, and enhance self-reliance while supporting farmers with efficient, crop-specific nutrition.

A Globally Verified Commitment to How We Operate
Earning a place among the world’s most trusted chemical companies through 
independently audited safety, environmental and stewardship practice.

n April 2026, Coromandel International was awarded the Responsible Care Certification by the Indian Chemical

The standard the industry is held to 
Responsible Care was established by the chemistry industry in Canada in 1985 and is today stewarded by the 
International Council of Chemical Associations. It is adopted by over 60 national associations across more than 70 
economies, and 90 of the world’s 100 largest chemical companies operate under its principles.
What separates the framework from voluntary commitments is the requirement for independently verified practice 
across the entire value chain. As multinational customers and global supply chain partners stringent procurement 
standards around environmental, social and governance performance, alignment with Responsible Care has shifted 
from preference to precondition.

Our Legacy and Evolution
Coromandel International Limited was incorporated in 1961 as Coromandel Fertilisers Limited, through a strategic 
collaboration between International Minerals and Chemical Corporation (USA), Chevron Chemical Company, and EID Parry. 
The Company commenced operations with the commissioning of its first complex fertiliser plant at Visakhapatnam in 1967, 
contributing meaningfully to India’s agricultural transformation during the Green Revolution.
Over the years, EID Parry progressively increased its shareholding, leading to Coromandel’s integration as a core company of 
the Murugappa Group, one of India’s most respected and diversified business conglomerates. This association strengthened 
Coromandel’s governance framework, long term vision, and its commitment to ethical and responsible business practices 
guided by the Group’s “Five Lights”.
From its origins as a fertiliser manufacturer, Coromandel has steadily evolved into an integrated agri solutions provider, 
expanding its capabilities across plant nutrients, crop protection, specialty and organic products, retail, and farm services. 
Today, its journey reflects a legacy of resilience and continuous transformation, focused on supporting Indian agriculture 
through innovation, scale, and sustainability.

Corporate Governance
The Company places Corporate Governance at the core of its operations, recognising it as fundamental to building stakeholder 
trust, ensuring long-term resilience, and enabling sustainable value creation. The Company’s governance framework is built 
on the principles of transparency, integrity, accountability, and ethical conduct, which guide decision-making and execution 
across all levels of the organisation.
The Company firmly believes that strong governance is essential to delivering enduring value for a wide range of stakeholders, 
including shareholders, investors, employees, suppliers, regulators, farmers, and the communities it serves. Governance is 
embedded as a strategic enabler, ensuring that business decisions and actions are consistently aligned with applicable legal, 
regulatory, and ethical standards.
The Board of Directors provides strategic oversight and direction, while monitoring the effectiveness of management in driving 
performance with clarity, discipline, and accountability. Through this Integrated Annual Report, the Company presents a 
transparent and comprehensive view of its financial performance, governance practices, and sustainability initiatives, enabling 
stakeholders to clearly understand its long-term vision and value creation approach.
The following are the seven key corporate governance focus areas 
that the Company strongly emphasises:
Transparency & Ethical Disclosure
Company is committed to transparent, timely and accurate disclosures across financial and non financial 
matters. The Company upholds the highest standards of ethical reporting, ensuring stakeholders receive 
clear, credible and decision useful information in line with applicable laws and regulations.
Proactive Risk Management
The Company follows a structured and forward‑looking risk management framework to identify, assess 
and mitigate strategic, operational, financial and emerging risks. This proactive approach strengthens 
resilience and supports informed decision‑making in a dynamic business environment.
Robust Internal Controls
Company maintains a strong system of internal controls to safeguard assets, ensure the integrity of 
financial reporting and promote compliance. Regular reviews, audits and process enhancements reinforce 
accountability and operational discipline across the organisation.
Excellence in Product & Service Quality
Quality is embedded across Company’s value chain from sourcing and manufacturing to service delivery. 
The Company continuously strengthens quality assurance systems to ensure consistent product 
performance, customer satisfaction and adherence to regulatory standards.

Risk Governance
Coromandel’s risk governance structure is led by the Board of Directors, which provides oversight on key risks that may 
influence the Company’s strategy, operations, financial position, compliance obligations and stakeholder relationships. The 
Board is supported by its committees, including the Risk Management Committee, Audit Committee and Corporate Social 
Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, each of which reviews risk matters relevant to its mandate.
The Risk Management Committee plays a critical role in reviewing the Company’s enterprise risk profile, mitigation progress 
and emerging areas of concern. It also monitors the effectiveness of the risk management framework and guides the 
prioritisation of risks that require senior management attention. The Audit Committee complements this oversight through its 
review of internal controls, audit observations and control-related corrective actions.
At the management level, the Executive Management Team, comprising the Managing Director, Executive Directors and 
CXOs, is responsible for translating Board-level risk priorities into business action. Business Heads, Corporate Functions and 
the EHS leadership team are accountable for identifying, assessing and managing risks within their respective areas. Unit-
level Safety and Sustainability Committees further support implementation at operating sites, particularly for risks linked to 
safety, environment, climate resilience, compliance and business continuity.

Integration of Climate and Nature-related Risks
Climate and nature related risks are increasingly relevant to Coromandel’s operations, supply chain and farmer 
facing businesses. The Company has therefore started integrating these risks into its Enterprise Risk Management 
framework, enabling them to be assessed alongside strategic, operational, regulatory and financial risks.
The climate risk assessment considers both physical risks such as water scarcity, drought, monsoon variability, 
flooding and extreme weather events, and transition risks such as regulatory changes, emissions-related expectations, 
energy transition, product stewardship and shifts towards greener chemistries. These risks are reviewed across 
short, medium and long-term horizons to understand their potential impact on manufacturing continuity, input 
costs, logistics, agricultural productivity and product portfolio decisions.
During the year, Coromandel also initiated nature-related risk assessment to better understand dependencies 
and impacts linked to water, soil health, biodiversity and ecosystem services. This included biodiversity screening, 
ecosystem services review and site-level assessment to identify areas where nature-related factors may influence 
operational resilience and long-term sustainability.
The insights from these assessments are being used to strengthen site level planning, water management, business 
continuity, energy efficiency, product development and farmer-focused solutions. As the framework matures, the 
Company aims to build a more location-specific understanding of climate and nature-related risks and convert these 
insights into focused mitigation actions.
Internal Control Systems
Coromandel’s risk management framework is supported by internal controls, policies and review mechanisms 
that help maintain process discipline across business and operating locations. These controls cover key areas 
such as financial reporting, statutory compliance, procurement, manufacturing operations, information systems, 
environmental performance, health and safety, and delegation of authority.
The Company follows defined procedures for approval, review and monitoring of critical business activities. Internal 
audits are conducted periodically to assess the adequacy of controls, identify process gaps and track corrective 
actions. Observations from audits and management reviews are placed before the relevant leadership teams and 
Board Committees, where required.
During the year, the Company continued to strengthen its risk management process through periodic risk reviews, 
business-level monitoring, site-level assessments and integration of climate, nature and resilience-related risks into 
the broader ERM process. The linkage between internal controls, risk ownership and mitigation tracking enables the 
Company to move from risk identification to practical action.

Materiality Assessment
Coromandel’s materiality assessment serves as a strategic 
anchor for its sustainability journey, enabling the Company 
to continuously align its priorities with a rapidly evolving 
business and stakeholder landscape. Conducted on a 
biannual basis, the assessment ensures that the Company’s 
focus areas remain relevant, forward-looking and responsive 
to emerging environmental, social and governance (ESG) 
risks and opportunities.
In FY 2025-26, the materiality assessment was undertaken 
with an enhanced level of accuracy, integrating multiple 
perspectives across the value chain and embedding both 
stakeholder relevance and business impact at the core 
of the evaluation. The exercise reflects Coromandel’s 
transition from a compliance driven approach towards a 
more strategically integrated and insight led sustainability 
framework, where material topics directly inform decision 
making, risk management and long-term value creation.
Rather than being a static output, the materiality process 
is designed as a dynamic and iterative mechanism, 
allowing the Company to periodically reassess its priorities 
considering changing regulatory expectations, industry 
developments, climate related risks, and socio-economic 
shifts within the agricultural ecosystem.
A comprehensive set of potential ESG topics was 
identified through a combination of global and 
sector-specific inputs. This included:
	» Benchmarking against leading peers within 
the industry
	» Mapping 
to 
internationally 
recognised 
sustainability frameworks
	» Reviewing internal policies, risk registers 
and strategic documents
	» Assessing sector-specific risks across the 
agricultural and agri-input value chain
This step ensured that the assessment began with a 
broad and inclusive universe of topics, capturing both 
current and emerging themes.
The refined topics were evaluated through structured 
stakeholder engagement, enabling the Company 
to capture diverse perspectives across internal and 
external stakeholder groups.
This step helped in:
	»
Understanding how different stakeholders 
prioritise ESG topics
	» Identifying areas of strong alignment as 
well as divergence
	» Surfacing emerging concerns that may not 
yet be fully integrated into business processes
The prioritised topics were mapped onto a materiality 
matrix, providing a visual representation of their 
significance across the two dimensions. This helped 
in clearly distinguishing:
	» High priority strategic topics
	» Areas 
requiring 
focused 
management 
attention
	» Emerging issues with potential future 
relevance

	» Stakeholder 
Importance: 
reflecting 
the 
relative priority assigned by stakeholders 
	» Business Impact: reflecting the potential 
influence 
on 
financial 
performance, 
operational continuity, risk exposure and 
long-term strategy

objective prioritisation of topics.
Based on the analysis, a refined set of material topics 
was finalised. These topics represent the issues 
that are most critical to both stakeholders and the

Coromandel’s business model, operational footprint 
and strategic priorities. Overlapping themes were 
consolidated and non relevant topics were filtered 
out, resulting in a focused set of issues that are 
meaningfully linked to the Company’s activities and 
impact areas.

Through FY 2025-26, Coromandel continued to strengthen 
the foundation of its manufacturing network, adding 
capacity in areas that consolidate competitive advantage 
and building capability in areas that accelerate future 
growth. Capital was deployed across four interlocking 
themes during the year, namely the strengthening of the 
crop protection franchise, the expansion of fertiliser capacity 
and raw material security, the deepening of the advanced 
and differentiated portfolio, and the long-term safeguarding 
of water resources.
Strengthening the crop protection
In a defining step for its crop protection business, 
Coromandel completed the acquisition of a 53.13% 
controlling stake in NACL Industries Limited for ₹820 
crore at ₹76.7 per share, following clearance from the 
Competition Commission of India in 2025. NACL brings to 
the portfolio an established branded formulation business 
in the domestic market, a technicals export base across key 
global markets and contract manufacturing relationships 
with leading global agrochemical companies, materially 
expanding Coromandel’s manufacturing footprint, product 
portfolio and operational scale in crop protection.
Manufacturing capability was further deepened for the 
manufacture of recently off patented fungicides, alongside 
a 9 KTPA technical plant at Dahej. Targeted capacity 
additions were also completed for key technical molecules 
at Ankleshwar and a herbicide block expansion at Sarigam.
Expanding fertiliser capacity and raw material 
security
At Kakinada, the Company advanced construction of a new 
NPK granulation train (Train H). On commissioning, Train 
H will add 7.5 lakh tonnes of annual capacity, taking the 
Kakinada site to 30 lakh tonnes per annum and positioning 
it among the largest phosphatic fertiliser complexes in 
India. The new train is being built using energy efficient, 
environmentally compliant technology and is designed to 
substitute DAP imports while improving balanced crop 
nutrition through complex NPKs.
Running in parallel, the previously announced backward 
integration investment of approximately ₹1,000 crore at 
Kakinada, comprising a 650 TPD phosphoric acid plant and 
a 2,000 TPD sulphuric acid plant, progressed as planned, 
this will bring all of Coromandel’s fertiliser manufacturing 
sites into a backward integrated configuration, reducing 
dependence on imports of intermediate raw materials.
Upstream raw material security was further reinforced 
through the commissioning of a fixed processing plant for 
Run of Mine (ROM) material at the Baobab Mining and 
Chemicals Corporation rock phosphate project in Senegal, 
in which Coromandel now holds a 53.8% stake. The 
fixed processing plant secures consistent rock phosphate 
feedstock for the Company’s phosphatic value chain and 
supports the upcoming phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada.
Deepening the advanced and differentiated 
portfolio
The advanced solutions portfolio was strengthened with 
a fully automated, energy efficient Nano Fertiliser Plant at 
Kakinada, featuring robotic bottling and an annual capacity 
of one crore bottles, with the platform designed to scale 
across multiple nano products. The differentiated portfolio 
was further extended through the commissioning of a 1.3 
lakh tonne Urea Single Super Phosphate facility at Nimrani 
in Madhya Pradesh, Udaipur, Rajasthan to manufacture 
Gromor Urea Super Phosphate (5:15:0:10), and the 
doubling of Bentonite Sulphur capacity at the Vizag unit to 
meet rising demand for secondary nutrients.
Securing water for the future
Reinforcing water security at one of its largest manufacturing 
hubs, Coromandel signed an agreement during the year 
with Veolia Water Technologies and Solutions (India) to 
expand seawater desalination capacity at Visakhapatnam 
from 6 MLD to 9 MLD, building on the 6 MLD plant 
commissioned in 2023. The expansion is being executed 
on a Build, Own, Operate model. On commissioning, the 
upgraded plant is expected to meet 60 to 70% of the site’s 
total water requirement, materially reducing dependence on 
freshwater sources and standing as a flagship achievement 
in operational sustainability and self-reliance.

Sustainable Chemistry in Action
In FY 2025-26, Coromandel continued to embed responsible 
chemistry practices across its innovation and manufacturing 
activities, with a focus on reducing environmental 
impact while maintaining product performance and 
process efficiency. These considerations are increasingly 
integrated at the design stage of products and processes, 
supporting the Company’s transition towards lower impact 
manufacturing approaches.
Within the Crop Protection Chemicals (CPC) business, 
the Company further strengthened its green chemistry 
capabilities by developing and improving a green 
synthetic process for the fungicidal technical Boscalid. The 
process is designed to be simple, resource efficient, and 
environmentally feasible, delivering higher yield and purity 
with reduced process intensity. During the year, the process 
was further refined, and an Indian patent application was 
filed, reinforcing both environmental stewardship and 
intellectual property protection.
In Nutrients, Coromandel continued its engagement with 
policy and institutional stakeholders, sharing inputs with 
the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) and 
the Department of Fertilizers (DoF) on the potential use of 
green ammonia in fertiliser production. These interactions 
reflect the Company’s intent to align with emerging low 
carbon technologies and contribute constructively to the 
development of sustainable fertiliser ecosystems.  
In Biologicals, the focus was on improving nutrient 
use efficiency and complementing the Company’s crop 
protection portfolio. The Biocharm platform enhances 
nutrient use efficiency, while BtK is used as a tank-mix 
partner that lowers the chemical dose required while 
maintaining efficacy. The operation itself is built around 
eco-friendly inputs, with sustainable raw materials, lower 
water and solvent consumption, and minimal discharge.
190+ patents filed and 64 granted represent cumulative intellectual property across Coromandel businesses, including 
Nutrients, CPC, and Bioproducts. The CPC figures represent business specific disclosures as per FY 2025-26 data.

Strategic Initiatives
Role mapping and organization restructuring 
From a role-mapping perspective, Coromandel undertook a comprehensive organisational restructuring exercise during the 
last financial year in partnership with a global consulting agency with the aim of strengthening its people processes, creating 
greater role clarity and building a scalable structure aligned with business growth. As part of this exercise, the Company’s 
earlier framework of 20 grades across 3 bands was revised to 19 grades across 6 bands.
Driven by senior leadership, the initiative was intended to make Coromandel a more agile organisation by redefining spans 
of control, roles and responsibilities and enabling faster career growth. Spanning several months, it involved extensive role 
mapping, outlier identification and benchmarking of the organisation structure against industry standards. Job evaluation was 
carried out using the Hays Methodology, a globally acclaimed and time-tested framework.
This restructuring has helped Coromandel establish a performance-driven culture, enable clearer career pathways, and create 
an organizational design that balances growth aspirations with operational efficiency.
Our Employee Value Proposition: “Enrich Your Journey”
To strengthen its employer brand, Coromandel articulated its Employee Value Proposition, “Enrich your journey”, a promise 
that shapes the experience it offers across the employee lifecycle. It is anchored in three cultural pillars, Enrich Your Code, 
Enrich Your Mind and Enrich Your Possibilities, uniting ethics, learning and growth into one holistic employee experience.
This stability in the overall turnover rate indicates:
	» Strong employee retention across key roles
	» Improved alignment between employee expectations and organisational offerings

Creating a Supportive and Connected Workplace 
At Coromandel, employee engagement and well-being are viewed as important enablers of operational performance, 
workforce stability and long-term growth. Given the Company’s presence across manufacturing units, field operations and 
corporate functions, delivering a consistent and inclusive employee experience remains a key priority.
During the reporting year, the Company continued to enhance employee experience through engagement initiatives, accessible 
communication platforms and well-being programmes designed to address the evolving needs of its workforce. Coromandel’s 
approach centres on creating a workplace where employees are encouraged to share feedback, participate in organisational 
processes and contribute meaningfully to team and business outcomes.
Underpinning this approach is the recognition that employee well-being directly influences productivity, engagement and 
workplace morale. Initiatives therefore focus on physical health, mental resilience and social security, while also helping 
employees manage their work-life priorities more effectively.

Measuring Engagement: A Complimentary Approach
Employee engagement is assessed through internal and external complementary mechanisms:

	»

Employee Well-being and Support 
Coromandel continues to place strong emphasis on employee well-being, recognising that a healthy, supported and engaged 
workforce is essential to sustained organisational performance. With a workforce of approximately ~6300 employees 
operating across manufacturing units, offices and field locations, the Company adopts a balanced approach that integrates 
policies, workplace flexibility and well-being initiatives to address diverse employee needs. 
The Company’s approach to well-being extends beyond traditional health measures to include physical, mental and social 
dimensions of employee welfare. During FY 2025-26, this commitment was reflected in over 100 well-being initiatives 
that reached employees across locations and functions. Participation across these programmes remained strong, with the 
Company’s flagship wellness platform, Bloom, recording around 75% participation and over 60% sustained engagement, 
indicating the growing adoption of healthier routines across the workforce.
The Company continues to focus on enabling policies that support employees through different life stages. Flexible working 
arrangements, childcare assistance post maternity leave and thoughtful leave policies have contributed to enhancing overall 
employee experience and accessibility to well-being resources.
Well-being in Action: Strengthening the ‘Bloom’ Platform 
As part of its continued focus on employee well-being, Coromandel has enhanced its flagship wellness platform, ‘Bloom’, 
which serves as a central pillar for driving employee participation, awareness and behavioural change across the organisation. 
Designed as an integrated well-being ecosystem, Bloom combines digital access with interventions to address multiple 
dimensions of employee health, including physical fitness, mental well-being and lifestyle management. The platform enables 
employees to engage with curated programmes, access expert-led sessions and adopt healthier routines in a structured and 
sustained manner. 
During FY 2025-26, the Company expanded the scope and reach of Bloom through targeted initiatives aimed at improving 
accessibility and driving deeper engagement across locations. Key initiatives under the Bloom programme included:
	»
Structured wellness sessions covering areas such as nutrition, physical fitness, stress management and mental 
well-being 
	»
Orientation and awareness sessions aimed at improving adoption and utilisation of the digital platform 
	»
Expert-led programmes encouraging employees to incorporate healthier routines into their daily lives 
	»
Health camps for employees ensuring continuous monitoring of health parameters. Unit level Medical Officers track 
employee health index periodically basis diagnostic testing and counsel employees on making lifestyle changes towards 
better health outcomes.
A recent addition to Bloom in line with women-centric initiatives was a Pregnancy Care program that women employees 
could sign up for, receiving dietary and fitness tips, easy access to specialists and groups where they could ask questions on 
their pregnancy journey and receive answers from medical experts. To further strengthen adoption, orientation and awareness 
sessions were conducted to familiarise employees with the platform and encourage regular participation. These efforts 
contributed to increased utilisation and visibility of the platform across the workforce.
Building Connection Through Transparent and Inclusive 
Communication
Coromandel’s multi-tier Communication Framework ensures employees across locations and functions have consistent access 
to leadership, open dialogue and organisational direction. The framework operates across three integrated layers: leadership 
connect, content and digital reach, and structured listening.
Leadership Connect 
Chronicle, the Managing Director’s quarterly townhall, brings together employees across locations through 
business updates, MD Award recognitions and open Q&A sessions. CHORD complements this by enabling 
employees to connect directly with the Managing Director over a phone call each quarter to share ideas, 
feedback, process improvements and appreciation. Business and Departmental Townhalls, led by Business and 
Department Heads, translate organisational priorities into relevant local action, with Unit level communication 
meets further strengthening frontline leadership visibility. 
Content and Digital Reach 
VOICE Magazine, the Company’s award-winning internal publication, shares updates, achievements and 
employee stories from across business units. Coromandel maintains active engagement through LinkedIn, 
Instagram, YouTube and Facebook, while CASPER, its AI-powered HR chatbot, provides employees with policy 
guidance, ensuring accessibility and responsiveness across the workforce. 
Listening and Feedback 
Employee feedback is gathered through structured channels including the Great Place to Work survey, HR 
Internal Perception Survey, Engagement Champion conversations and HR Connects at locations/units. Insights 
are translated into action planning meetings with managers, monitored by the HR SPOCs at locations for 
accountability and timely action. A trained network of Engagement Champions facilitates ongoing team-level 
conversations across functions and locations. 
A key highlight of the year was the 22-day “BLOOMathon” step challenge, designed to promote physical activity 
and encourage sustained behavioural change. The initiative encouraged employees to achieve a daily target of 8,000 
steps and witnessed:
	»
Approximately 75% employee participation, reflecting strong engagement across functions and locations. 
	»
Over 60% sustained participation, indicating consistent involvement and the adoption of healthier habits.
Employee Benefits and Social Security 
Coromandel continues to provide a comprehensive benefits framework aimed at ensuring financial security, risk protection 
and long-term well-being for its employees. The Company’s approach is designed to go beyond statutory requirements, 
offering a balanced mix of protection-oriented and long-term financial benefits that support employees across different 
stages of their careers. 
All permanent employees are covered under a range of benefit programmes that contribute to their financial stability and 
overall well-being. These include accident insurance coverage, retirement provisions and schemes aligned with gratuity and 
superannuation benefits, providing support both during active employment and over the long term. This framework is further 
reinforced by statutory schemes such as the Employee Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI), along with other group insurance 
programmes. Coverage is extended in line with defined eligibility criteria and employee grades, so that benefits remain 
equitable and relevant across the organisation.
Leave, Flexibility and Life-Stage Support
Coromandel continues to strengthen its human capital practices by embedding flexibility, inclusivity and life-stage support 
into its workplace framework. The Company recognises that employees operate within diverse personal and professional 
contexts and therefore require a work environment that is both structured and adaptable to evolving needs. Reflecting this, 
its leave and flexibility framework is designed not merely as a compliance requirement but as a strategic enabler of sustained 
employee engagement, career continuity and workforce resilience. By integrating statutory provisions with progressive policies 
and practical support mechanisms, the Company helps employees navigate critical life events while remaining meaningfully 
connected to the organisation.
A key component of the Company’s framework is Group Personal Accident Insurance, which provides compensation 
for total permanent disablement equivalent to 50 times the monthly gross salary for eligible employees. In addition, 
support is extended in cases of temporary disablement, including weekly compensation of ₹15,000 for a period of up 
to 104 weeks, ensuring income continuity during periods of absence.
In parallel, the Company offers retirement and long-term savings benefits, with Provident Fund coverage extended 
to all permanent employees. Superannuation Fund (SAF) benefits are available to eligible employees based on 
individual participation, supporting long-term financial planning and retirement preparedness. Employees are also 
covered under gratuity-linked benefits, where entitlements are linked to the completed service period. In certain 
cases, additional provisions extend benefits to cover the remaining service period up to the age of 58 years for eligible 
employees who have opted for SAF, providing enhanced financial security to employees and their families. The Group 
Term life Insurance policy offers income protection for family and covers all employee categories including contract 
labour, while the Benevolent Fund scheme offers immediate assistance in case of an employee’s death while in service.

The Company’s process safety framework is strengthened through a Risk-Based Process Safety (RBPS) approach, focused 
on five core enablers:
Process Safety Management and Responsible Operations
For Coromandel, process safety is central to responsible manufacturing. The Company’s operations involve chemicals and 
critical utilities such as ammonia, sulphuric acid, phosphoric acid, high-pressure steam, instrument air and vacuum systems, 
making disciplined risk management essential for protecting people, communities, assets and the environment.

In practice, this approach is implemented through hazard studies, standard operating procedures, inspection and maintenance 
systems, management of change, permit-to-work controls, emergency preparedness and incident investigation. Employees 
involved in process operations and high-risk work are trained to understand process hazards, follow defined procedures and 
respond effectively to abnormal situations.
Notice and Consultation on Operational Changes
When significant operational changes arise, the Company follows a systematic approach to communication and compliance. A 
minimum notice period is provided to employees in line with applicable statutory requirements, typically ranging between 21 
to 42 days depending on the nature of the change, employee category and regulatory provisions, ensuring that employees are 
adequately informed and supported during any transition. Where applicable, these provisions are aligned with agreements 
established with trade unions and employee representatives, so that workforce-related decisions are undertaken in 
consultation and in accordance with mutually agreed terms. During FY 2025-26, no significant operational changes requiring 
advance workforce notice arose.
Coromandel has institutionalised a Process Safety Management System (PSMS) across its plants to identify, 
evaluate, and control process-related hazards. The system is embedded into plant operations, engineering practices, 
and high-risk activities, ensuring that process risks are considered at each stage of operational decision-making.

For an agri-inputs business, the most valuable assets rarely appear on a balance sheet. They are the trust of the farmer who 
returns to a Gromor store season after season, the credibility earned over thousands of field visits, and the strength of the 
networks—producer organisations, agronomists, retailers and rural communities—through which knowledge and confidence 
flow. Relationship Capital is our measure of these bonds: the depth of our connection to the farming communities we serve,

physically present in the farmer’s field, responsive to local conditions, and accountable for the results we help deliver.
Strong relationships begin with understanding the land, and over the year we conducted 94,935 soil tests and supported 
soil health interventions across nearly 1.5 crore acres. A team of over 100 agronomists carried this advisory directly to the 
field, executing more than 2.24 lakh field visits and 9,358 farmer meetings, while active partnerships with 1,104 Farmer 
Producer Organisations extended our technology and advisory deeper into farming communities. Building on this foundation, 
we brought precision agriculture within reach of the smallholder: through the Gromor Drive commercial drone service we 
covered 1.30 lakh acres, and the Namo Drone Didi programme empowered women in agri-tech to execute a further 55,000 
acres of drone spraying. Our Gromor Gram model-village initiative scaled across 102 villages spanning 92 districts in 12 
states, demonstrating integrated, technology-led farming at the community level.

new store a day, opening 320 outlets to expand the network of 1200+ stores. The proximity translated directly into trust: the 
Gromor brand’s Net Promoter Score rose sharply from 51 to 71, a clear signal that farmers increasingly see Coromandel not

interventions across nearly 1.5 crore acres of farmland.

deficiencies, improve fertiliser-use efficiency, strengthen soil 
health and enhance farm productivity over the long term.

Creating Safe Spaces for Health & Dignity: A DEI 
Journey with the Transgender Community
For many in the transgender community, healthcare is 
not simply a question of access but of dignity. Clinics that 
should offer care frequently become spaces of discomfort, 
judgement and avoidance, with the result that medical 
needs are deferred until they harden into crises. As 
part of its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment, 
Coromandel International chose to engage with this reality 
directly, beginning not with a programme design but with 
a conversation. Representatives from the transgender 
community were invited to the Company’s offices to share 
their lived experiences, and what emerged most sharply 
was the discrimination routinely encountered in healthcare 
settings, a barrier that, more than any clinical or financial 
constraint, was keeping community members away from 
timely medical support. 
This insight became the design brief. Rather than 
directing community members towards existing facilities, 
Coromandel brought healthcare to spaces where they could 
engage without fear or bias, organising comprehensive 
health camps across Chennai city and Ennore. Through 
these camps, over 170 transgender individuals received 
complete health checkups, including essential screenings 
for cancer and HIV and AIDS, services that, despite being 
clinically routine, are rarely accessed comfortably by the 
community. What makes this intervention meaningful is not 
its scale but its starting point: by listening before designing, 
and by treating dignity as the precondition rather than the 
byproduct of care, Coromandel’s DEI journey illustrates how 
genuine inclusion is built, not as a statement of intent, but 
as a series of safe, respectful spaces where access is no 
longer mediated by stigma.
Project Mamatha: Strengthening Grassroots 
Care through Anganwadi Transformation
In rural India, the Anganwadi is far more than a building. It is 
the first point of contact between the public health system 
and the most vulnerable, namely pregnant women, infants, 
young children and adolescent girls. From early pregnancy 
detection and maternal health monitoring to immunisation, 
nutrition supplementation, preschool education for children 
aged three to five and counselling for adolescent girls, the 
Anganwadi quietly carries a vast share of the country’s 
grassroots care responsibility. Yet many of these centres 
operate from neglected premises that erode their own 
effectiveness, discouraging the very families they were 
built to serve. Recognising this gap, Coromandel launched 
Project Mamatha, a CSR initiative aimed not at building 
parallel infrastructure, but at revitalising what already 
exists at the heart of the community. 
Under the initiative, seven Anganwadi centres across the villages of Valasapakala and Vakalapudi have been comprehensively 
renovated, with clean toilets and running water, expanded infrastructure to accommodate growing needs, secure boundary 
walls protecting kitchens and premises, and vibrant wall paintings that turn each centre into a child friendly learning 
environment. Each renovated centre now serves an average of 150 beneficiaries per month across mothers, pregnant women, 
children and adolescent girls, with the initiative estimated to benefit close to 12,000 individuals over time. Beyond the visible 
upgrade, the deeper change is in trust: attendance has risen, families are accessing services more actively, children are turning 
up for preschool routines, and adolescent girls are participating with noticeably greater confidence. By choosing to strengthen 
public infrastructure rather than substitute for it, Project Mamatha shows how thoughtful CSR can amplify the reach of the 
state, restoring dignity to spaces that anchor the earliest, and most consequential, years of a child’s life.

At Coromandel, our sense of responsibility has always reached beyond the fields we serve and the nutrients we provide, into

The institution began modestly in 2015 as a small medical centre in a rented building, with a few rooms, basic facilities and

place dependable medical care within reach of the underserved.
Over the past decade, that beginning has grown into a premier 60-bed, multi-specialty institution. The hospital was upgraded

the care available locally. Today, Coromandel Hospital has served more than 3.44 lakh patients across the Kakinada, Dr. B.R. 
Ambedkar Konaseema and East Godavari districts, with over 600 individuals placing their trust in the institution each day—
from new mothers and elderly patients in chronic care to families navigating critical moments of their lives.

long and exhausting journeys to metropolitan centres. The hospital introduced the region’s first helium-free MRI—not as a 
showpiece, but in the belief that early, precise diagnosis saves lives and that a farming family in Konaseema deserves the 
same standard of imaging as anyone in a major city. This is supported by three fully equipped modular operation theatres, 
an eight-bed Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU), a dedicated Surgical Intensive Care Unit (SICU) and a specialised Neonatal 
Intensive Care Unit (NICU).

in moments that matter most, remain its most valuable asset. To every family within its 100-kilometre service radius, the

above wellbeing.

services, so that no one in the region is ever forced to choose between their health and their savings. Sustained by care,

UDAN Masti Ki Pathshala: Giving Wings to Childhood in Migrant Communities
In the industrial corridors of Ankleshwar GIDC, where migrant families from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat 
power factories and construction sites, education had quietly slipped to the margins of childhood. The seed for UDAN was 
sown during a Women’s Day celebration at Coromandel’s Ankleshwar Plant, when Maladevi, a widowed migrant worker, 
asked a deceptively simple question: could something be done to help educate their children? A community visit revealed that 
her concern was far from isolated. More than 150 children in the settlement were either out of school, irregular in attendance, 
or at risk of dropping out, hemmed in by language barriers, financial constraints and the absence of a nearby government 
primary school.
In response, Coromandel International, in partnership with Swadeep Foundation, conceived UDAAN, Masti Ki Pathshala as 
an ecosystem led intervention rather than a one off enrolment drive. Built on a dual strategy of access and learning, the 
programme established Learning Centres within the migrant settlements themselves, replacing rote pedagogy with activity 
based, joyful learning focused on foundational literacy, numeracy and school readiness. What began with three centres 
grew organically to six on the strength of community demand alone. Over the year, 489 children were enrolled, more than 
350 attended regularly, and 30 children, many for the first time in their lives, transitioned into mainstream schools through 
sustained counselling, document facilitation and system navigation by the team. 
What distinguishes UDAN is its design philosophy: learning is taken to where children live, parents are engaged as partners 
rather than passive recipients, and barriers that conventional programmes often overlook, such as language exclusion, migrant 
identity, low parental literacy and fragile home learning environments, are addressed directly. For Coromandel, the initiative 
illustrates how CSR can move beyond infrastructure or service delivery to respond to deeply embedded social inequities 
through empathy led design, gradually disrupting an intergenerational pattern of educational exclusion. In neighbourhoods 
where schooling once felt distant, it now exists within reach, and a widow’s question is being answered not through charity, 
but through opportunity.

In government schools across India, persistent teacher shortages frequently leave classrooms half attended and young 
learners waiting, a structural gap in which learning quietly slips off course. Coromandel’s employee volunteering programme

In Indian classrooms, chemistry is too often experienced as a subject to be memorised rather than understood, a wall of 
formulae and reactions disconnected from the world students live in. Prayog Utsav, Chemistry & Its Fundamentals, launched

science and engineering concepts through engaging, hands on models has matured into a layered programme combining

Problem to Prototype, and Fun with Nano Chemistry, domains that mirror the very challenges India’s next generation of 
scientists and engineers will be asked to solve. By creating a visible stage where curiosity is rewarded and experimentation 
celebrated, Prayog Utsav does more than teach chemistry. It reframes it, turning a feared subject into a familiar one, and a 
textbook discipline into a tool for thinking, building and imagining.

vigil, one undertaken in the dark hours, by ordinary people, 
on behalf of lives that cannot speak for themselves.

Case Study
Watershed Development and Community Livelihood Enhancement 
The five villages of Kevra Khurd, Chansda, Jamar Kotda, Umarda and Bedwas are located approximately 35 kilometres from 
Udaipur city, spread across the Sarada, Kurabad and Girwa community development blocks of Udaipur district in Rajasthan. 
Collectively, these villages span an area of 3,876 hectares, of which only 952 hectares are cultivable and 149 hectares fall 
under forest cover. The remaining land is either unproductive wasteland or otherwise unsuitable for agricultural use.
The communities residing in these villages are predominantly tribal households. With a combined population of approximately 
9,610 people across 1,908 households, their livelihoods have historically depended on rainfed agriculture and, to a lesser 
extent, labour from nearby mining operations. Annual rainfall in the region averages just 637 mm, which is both insufficient 
and highly erratic in its distribution across the year. 
The consequences of this dependence on rainfall, without adequate water storage or irrigation infrastructure, have been 
significant. Agricultural productivity has remained persistently low, incomes unstable, and a large proportion of working 
age adults have been compelled to migrate seasonally in search of wage employment. Degraded natural resources, limited 
groundwater recharge and the absence of efficient farming practices have further compounded these challenges, leaving 
communities in a cycle of vulnerability that is difficult to break without structured, long-term support.
Recognising the scale of these challenges, Coromandel initiated a watershed development programme in March FY2025 in 
partnership with the Watershed Organisation Trust (WOTR), a credible and experienced implementing organisation in the 
space of integrated natural resource management. The project is designed to run through FY2027 and targets an augmentation 
of 90,000 kilolitres of water harvesting potential across the five project villages, directly benefitting the communities living in 
and around these geographies.
Our Approach
The project adopts an integrated approach, combining 
physical 
infrastructure 
creation 
with 
agricultural 
improvement and community institution strengthening. 
Rather than addressing any single constraint in isolation, 
the programme works across four interconnected areas 
simultaneously, ensuring that gains in one area reinforce 
progress in another.
Water Resource Development
The primary focus of the project has been on creating and 
restoring water harvesting structures to improve both 
the storage and the management of available water. This 
includes de-siltation of existing check dams, renovation 
of traditional wells, construction of new check dams and 
development of earthen dams. These structures serve a 
dual purpose, by storing surface runoff during the monsoon 
season and simultaneously support groundwater recharge, 
which benefits the wider area during dry months.
Climate Resilient Agriculture
Alongside water infrastructure, farmers have been supported in transitioning towards more productive and resilient farming 
practices. This includes the distribution of improved seed varieties of maize and wheat, provision of sprinkler irrigation systems 
for more efficient water use and access to spray pumps for crop protection. The establishment of Equipment Bank Centres 
(EBC) has enabled farmers to share machinery and reduce individual input costs, making modern farming tools accessible 
even to smallholders who would otherwise be unable to afford them.
Community Participation and Governance
A distinguishing feature of this programme is the active involvement of communities in every stage of the project. 
Village Development Committees (VDC) across all five villages have been strengthened to take ownership of planning, 
implementation and monitoring of activities. Water User Groups (WUG) have been constituted and trained to manage 
equitable water distribution at the local level. This approach ensures that interventions are not donor dependent and that 
communities themselves become the custodians of the assets created.
Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer
Structured training programmes, farmer demonstrations and exposure visits to successful models in other regions have been 
conducted throughout the project period. These initiatives have equipped community members, particularly farmers and 
women, with the knowledge and confidence to adopt improved practices independently. The goal is not just immediate 
impact but a lasting shift in how communities manage their resources and livelihoods.

A fertiliser or crop protection product does not stop

Coromandel evaluates and controls product related risks 
from concept to end of life, covering the full chain from 
research and development through manufacture, transport,

journey from the outset.

Inside the boundary of one of India’s largest phosphatic fertilizer facilities, more than 5,000 birds gather every season. Storks 
and herons’ nest in the avenue trees lining the factory road. Migrants travelling thousands of kilometres from Siberia, the 
Arctic, and Central Asia arrive each winter. A Near Threatened species found nowhere else in the Kakinada region, including 
the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary, returns here year after year. None of this is accidental. It is the harvest of more than two 
decades of deliberate ecological stewardship.
A Sensitive Landscape, A Deliberate Choice
The 696-acre facility sits on the eastern coast of Andhra Pradesh, beside the East Godavari Riverine Estuarine Ecosystem 
along the Central Asian Flyway, one of the world’s great bird migration routes. These wetlands face relentless pressure from 
aquaculture, infrastructure, habitat disturbance, and poaching, threatening species such as the Spot-billed Pelican, Painted 
Stork, and Oriental Darter. Of the 696 acres, barely 100 acres support the manufacturing plant, utilities, and offices. The rest 
belongs to nature.
Birds Paradise: Where Industry and Nature Grow Together at 
Coromandel International Limited, Kakinada
A 300-acre green belt of native species, shaped with the Andhra Pradesh Forest Department, anchors the habitat, supported 
by a 25-acre constructed lake replenished with treated water and stocked with fish seed, and a 15-acre restored forest. The 
nursery, running since 1987, raises 30,000 plants annually across 160 species to renew the green belt. The factory silenced 
its daily siren, posted silent zone boards at nesting clusters, fenced key habitats, deployed round the clock antipoaching 
security, and engaged local fishermen through non fishing zones. A dedicated five-member Birds Conservation Committee, 
spanning ornithology, environmental engineering, horticulture, veterinary science, and civil infrastructure, oversees annual 
Waterbird Censuses and continuous monitoring with the UNDP GEF EGREE project. Coromandel has committed to green belt 
and wetland upkeep, sustained consistently across more than two decades.
